applies_why: The judge text grounds STANDS on cited verses or rows not stating the challenged claim, which is the kind of ground K-S2 forbids.
quote: the challenger's seed and father rows in DR3 do not state Joseph begat Jesus
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: a single verse does not state a link or its contrary. Readings weighed: narrow—only an isolated single verse’s silence is barred; broad—any cited verse’s or row’s silence is barred as a ground for STANDS. I applied the broad reading because the judge uses the rows’ non-statement as support.
why: D6 expressly makes the challenger’s rows not stating 'Joseph begat Jesus' part of the ground for STANDS, which K-S2 forbids.
